supplemental_assessments.exact_task: A convex mirror has a real object at d=30 cm and an object–image separation of 42 cm. The object moves to a position where its upright image is half its height. Infer the focal magnitude, new object position and separation; check whether an observer's claim that a larger image means a larger separation is consistent.
supplemental_assessments.protected_work: Model signed object–image separation, distinguish it from image position and magnification, and use independent observations to test mirror parameters.
supplemental_assessments.shortest_route: Initial v=42−30=12 cm. 1/F=1/v−1/d=1/12−1/30=1/20, so F=20 cm. m=F/(F+d)=1/2 gives d=20 cm; v=10 cm; S=30 cm. m initially 0.4, rises to 0.5, but S falls 42→30 cm. Claim false.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Choose signed convex mirror model plus separation, not plane-mirror shortcut.

representation_translation.evidence: Translate separation and size observations into v and m with consistent axes.

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Infer focal magnitude, solve second object position, compare both observables.

algebra_computational_load.evidence: Routine reciprocal and ratio arithmetic required.

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Distinguish apparent size from separation and check real-object domain.

supplemental_assessments.exact_task: An optical bench reports an object 8 cm beyond the front focus and an image 18 cm beyond the rear focus of a converging lens. The object–screen distance is reported as 48 cm. Determine whether all three observations can hold for one ideal lens, then state the predicted magnification and correct total distance if the offsets are accurate.
supplemental_assessments.protected_work: Combine focal-reference offsets with the real-conjugate constraint and independently check the resulting global image geometry.
supplemental_assessments.shortest_route: F=√(8×18)=12 cm. p=20 cm,q=30 cm, so D=50 cm, not 48; |m|=30/20=1.5, inverted. Both p,q>F and 1/p+1/q=1/12. The three observations are inconsistent.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Select focal-offset and conjugate constraint rather than treating offsets as pole distances.

representation_translation.evidence: Translate between focus-relative and lens-relative measurements.

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Infer F, conjugates, magnification, and independently test reported separation.

algebra_computational_load.evidence: Routine square root and arithmetic required.

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Real-conjugate assumptions and incompatible data must be checked.

supplemental_assessments.exact_task: A beam enters a transparent wedge normally through a face with tangent heading 35°; it next hits a silvered face whose tangent heading φ is unknown and then a second silvered face of tangent heading 80°. Its final direction must be downward (270°). Determine the possible φ modulo 180° from direction constraints and explain why direction alone does not certify finite-segment interception.
supplemental_assessments.protected_work: Construct the two-reflection heading composition and enforce the stated exit direction, not a memorized prism angle.
supplemental_assessments.shortest_route: θ₀=35−90=−55°. First reflection θ₁=2φ+55°. Second θ₂=160−(2φ+55)=105−2φ. Set θ₂≡270 (mod 360), so 2φ≡195 (mod 360), φ≡97.5° (mod 180). Check θ₁=250°, θ₂=−90°≡270°. Actual segment interception and reflecting side must be checked separately.

supplemental_assessments.exact_task: A thin converging lens of f=12 cm at x=0 images a 2 cm tall real object at x=−20 cm. Two possible plane-mirror placements perpendicular to the axis are x=22 cm and x=14 cm. For each placement find the would-be lens image, first return focus coordinate and whether it is reached before the lens; give signed transverse height only for a valid first return focus.
supplemental_assessments.protected_work: Combine first conjugate, mirror transformation and actual return ordering before reporting the final image and its height.
supplemental_assessments.shortest_route: q=12×20/(20−12)=30 cm, m=−30/20=−1.5, h_i=−3 cm. At M=22, x_R=44−30=14 cm: valid real focus before return reaches lens, h_i=−3 cm. supplemental_assessments.exact_task: A thin converging lens F=12 cm is followed by a perpendicular plane mirror. With object p=18 cm the central ray retraces; the operator claims all rays strike the mirror normally if the mirror is placed at the image plane. Test the claim, identify the required object position for all paraxial rays to strike normally, and explain whether the mirror distance then matters.
supplemental_assessments.protected_work: Determine whether the stated all-ray normal incidence and retracing can hold, not just whether the central ray returns.
supplemental_assessments.shortest_route: p=18 gives q=36 cm, so noncentral rays converge to that plane obliquely. Central ray normal does not imply all rays normal. For all rays normal to perpendicular mirror, output must be axial and parallel, requiring p=F=12 cm. Mirror axial distance does not affect normal incidence for collimated rays, subject to aperture.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Choose collimation/normal-incidence model rather than central ray alone.

representation_translation.evidence: Translate axial and off-axis ray conditions to conjugate geometry.

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Calculate first image, test claimed normal incidence, infer focal-plane requirement.

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Central versus all-ray retracing and finite aperture are decisive.

supplemental_assessments.exact_task: Two point sources are 30 cm apart on opposite sides of an ideal converging lens of f=12 cm. Their images are at the same finite global position. Find both source distances, identify which gives the real image, and verify the common global coordinate when the farther source is on the left.
supplemental_assessments.protected_work: Translate two local lens axes to one laboratory axis, derive the shared-image constraint and reject degenerate solutions.
supplemental_assessments.shortest_route: Let p+r=30. Equality of x_L=Fp/(p−F) and x_R=−Fr/(r−F) gives pr=FS/2=180. Roots z=(30±√180)/2≈21.708,8.292 cm. Farther p>12 forms real image x≈26.83 cm; nearer right r<12 gives local v≈−26.83 cm, global x≈+26.83 cm. Both coincide; reversing assignments flips global side.

supplemental_assessments.exact_task: A convex spherical mirror has radius magnitude 48 cm. A real object is measured 72 cm from the virtual focus. A report says the virtual image is 8 cm from the pole. Construct a signed position-line with object, pole, image, focus and centre; calculate the correct image offset from focus and decide whether the report confused the two reference points.
supplemental_assessments.protected_work: Convert measurements relative to focus and pole into one signed position-line representation and use it to identify inconsistent experimental claims.
supplemental_assessments.shortest_route: F=24, C=+48. y=72 implies u=−48. z=F²/y=576/72=8 cm from focus, so v=+16 cm from pole. Report's 8 cm is focus offset, not pole distance. Order O −48,P 0,I +16,F +24,C +48. Check 1/24=−1/48+1/16.

representation_translation.evidence: Construct a signed position line from reference-relative measurements.

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Infer F,d,z,v, compare report and verify signed law.

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Focus versus pole origin is decisive.

supplemental_assessments.exact_task: An optical adjustment screw of pitch 0.8 mm/turn changes object–lens separation; the thin lens has F=48 mm. A real screen image changes from four times to twice object height. Calculate the number of complete turns and required relative screen travel; decide whether a screen rigidly fixed to the lens could stay sharp throughout.

supplemental_assessments.shortest_route: p₁=48(1+1/4)=60 mm, p₂=48(1+1/2)=72 mm; Δp=12 mm, N=15 turns. q₁=48(1+4)=240 mm, q₂=48(1+2)=144 mm; Δq=−96 mm. A screen fixed relative to lens cannot satisfy both sharp conjugates.

supplemental_assessments.exact_task: Two rays travel from P=(−4,0) and Q=(0,−4) toward the origin, respectively east and north. A single plane mirror through the origin allegedly sends the east-going ray north and the north-going ray east. Draw both directed rays, infer the mirror line, then decide whether a one-sided mirror can reflect both rays from the same physical face.
supplemental_assessments.protected_work: Reconstruct a common reflecting-line orientation from multiple directed ray observations, then test whether a finite mirror can realize the observed paths.
supplemental_assessments.shortest_route: Both heading pairs imply φ=45° mod 180°, so mirror y=x. But P lies on y−x=+4 and Q on y−x=−4, opposite sides. Thus the direction equations agree while a one-sided mirror cannot accept both incident rays. A two-sided ideal reflecting plane could.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Choose plane reflection rather than rotate ray independently.

representation_translation.evidence: Translate two coordinate paths into directed rays and a common mirror line.

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Infer common orientation, then test incident-side compatibility.

algebra_computational_load.evidence: Only signs and elementary geometry; no material algebra.

supplemental_assessments.exact_task: Three labelled markers are A=(1,1), B=(4,1), C=(2,3). An image report gives A′=(−1,−1), B′=(−4,−1), C′=(−2,−3), and claims one mirror created it. A second report gives A″=(−1,1), B″=(−4,1), C″=(−2,3). Justify which report can be a single reflection and identify the simplest transformation for the other. Use signed orientation as evidence.
supplemental_assessments.protected_work: Use an oriented non-collinear configuration to distinguish a single reflection from a rotation or even number of reflections, rather than rely on verbal left/right labels.
supplemental_assessments.shortest_route: Original signed double area det(B−A,C−A)=6. First report vectors (−3,0),(−1,−2) give +6: orientation preserved, impossible for one reflection of non-collinear labelled points; it is a 180° rotation about origin (or two perpendicular reflections). Second gives det((−3,0),(−1,2))=−6, and all points satisfy x→−x, y unchanged, so reflection across x=0.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Select reflection versus proper rotation criterion.

representation_translation.evidence: Translate labelled coordinate observations to oriented vector pairs.

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Calculate orientation, reject one reflection, identify transformation.

algebra_computational_load.evidence: Routine determinants with signs are material.

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Non-collinear labelled points required; an arrow alone is insufficient.

supplemental_assessments.exact_task: A monochromatic beam enters a transparent material from air. The measured wavelength changes from 720 nm to 480 nm. A technician records the incoming angle as 30° to the normal and the outgoing angle as 19.47°, but does not say whether the latter is to the normal or surface. Determine which interpretation is consistent, then predict the speed ratio and explain whether a second normally incident beam alone can verify the index.
supplemental_assessments.protected_work: Combine independent wavelength and angular observations to identify a consistent optical-index model and reject an ambiguous angle convention.
supplemental_assessments.shortest_route: Frequency unchanged gives n₂/n₁=720/480=1.5 and v₂/v₁=2/3. Snell gives sin r=sin30/1.5=1/3, r≈19.47° to the normal. If measured to surface, normal angle would be 70.53°, inconsistent. Normal beam remains collinear regardless of index ratio; directional measurement alone cannot verify n.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Select stationary-interface model and conservation of frequency.

representation_translation.evidence: Translate wavelength ratio and ambiguous angular reference into one physical model.

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Infer index, predict angle, test alternative convention and normal-incidence identifiability.

algebra_computational_load.evidence: Routine ratio and sine calculations are necessary.

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Angle-reference ambiguity or forbidden transmission changes validity.
